extracted.intended_audience: mathematics education researchers and undergraduate calculus instructors designing instruction for limits/Taylor series
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and facilitating classroom activities in which students reinvent formal definitions of sequence, series, and Taylor series convergence through graphical, informal, and formulaic reasoning. Focus is on supports, prompts, and representations that enable students to coordinate ε, N, x, and n.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide timely instructional guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The timely instructional guidance provided to the students during the teaching experiment successfully supported them engaging these challenges and their subsequent reinvention of these definitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructors should intervene at strategic moments to surface problematic issues and scaffolding needs; timely prompts and probes help students overcome difficulties such as coordinating ε, N, x, and n. Anti-pattern: withholding help until after students are irretrievably off-track.

rubrics_metrics.name: Have students produce graphs of series and Taylor series convergence
rubrics_metrics.description: The facilitators having students produce graphs of series and Taylor series convergence gave students a reference point for which they could refer to during the construction of their definitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use student-generated graphs as shared artifacts to ground discussion and to link visual and formal accounts. Example: graphs of partial sums and Taylor polynomial approximations that students can point to while articulating definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt production of graphs without focusing on specific formulas
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance provided by the facilitators suggesting to the students that they produce series graphs without focusing on particular formulas freed the students from being constrained by attempting to recall specific series formulas and allowed them to produce more series graphs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage generic/qualitative graph construction rather than immediately invoking formulas; this reduces cognitive load and supports structural reasoning. Anti-pattern: insisting on formula recall before conceptual graphed reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Act as conflict producers (generate productive cognitive conflict)
rubrics_metrics.description: The facilitators served as eventual conflict producers by having the students produce Taylor series formulas that led to their eventual recognition that the tail of the series had value and therefore, a Taylor polynomial and the approximated function in these cases could not be identical over an interval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliberately design prompts that create tensions between students' informal beliefs and formal consequences (e.g., compute tails to show remaining nonzero terms). Use conflicts to motivate refinement of concepts. Anti-pattern: smoothing over or avoiding disconfirming evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use vertical number lines to represent pointwise approximations
rubrics_metrics.description: The guidance to produce and unpack vertical number line graphs supported students in seeing the graphs of Taylor series as comprised of convergent series at each x-value where N is dependent upon x as well as ε.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduce vertical number-line depictions (one per x-value) to make explicit that for each fixed x there is a sequence of partial-sum approximations and an N that depends on x and ε. Example: multiple vertical lines under a function showing Sn(x) approaching f(x) for different x.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage prior activity (sequence convergence) to scaffold new definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: We claim that the prior activity of defining sequence convergence became a means for supporting the students' definitions of series and Taylor series convergence as they recognized similarities between sequences, series, and Taylor series convergence in the context of their graphs and their definitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sequence convergence tasks can be used as a conceptual basis to transfer structures (ε, N, quantifiers, approximations) to series and Taylor series contexts. Design lessons to explicitly map corresponding elements across tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage and develop approximation terminology/scheme
rubrics_metrics.description: The students' emerging approximation scheme greatly supported the students in meaningfully recognizing similarities between definitions and interpreting components within a definition. Approximation terminology (partial sums as approximations, U − an's as errors, ε as error bounds) helped bridge gaps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote consistent use of approximation language (approximation, error, error bound) across sequences, series, and Taylor polynomials to help students abstract structural similarities. Example: treating partial sums, terms, and Taylor polynomials uniformly as approximations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probe and elicit students' articulation of variable/quantifier roles
rubrics_metrics.description: After production of their definitions, the facilitators probed the students' understandings and the students described the roles for x, ε, N, and n consistent with formal theory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use questioning to have students explain the roles and interdependencies of x, ε, N, and n (e.g., how N depends on x and ε, why 'for all x' placement matters). Scoring note: correct responses should reflect formal relationships (pointwise dependence of N on x).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use comparisons between series and Taylor series to highlight structural differences
rubrics_metrics.description: Students compared series and Taylor series focusing on the influence of the independent variable found in Taylor series but absent in series (e.g., 'series converge to a number but Taylor series converge to a function').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompt explicit comparisons (graphical and conceptual) to make salient that series target numbers while Taylor series target functions and that the independent variable introduces x-dependence of N. Anti-pattern: treating Taylor series as the same object as ordinary numeric series without addressing x.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design reinvention tasks that allow students to construct definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Students reinvented and unpacked the formal definition of series and pointwise convergence within a short time through iterative refinement, grappling with issues like placement of 'for all x' and N's dependence on x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create tasks that require students to iteratively propose, test, and revise candidate definitions (reinvention), supported by representations and facilitator prompts. Benefit: students build understanding through resolving identified problems rather than being presented the formal definition up-front.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use explicit computation/formula generation to reveal remainder/tail significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Facilitators had students produce Taylor series formulas that led to recognition that the tail of the series had value and that finite Taylor polynomials are merely approximations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include activities that compute explicit series and examine tails/remainders to counter misconceptions that finite polynomials become exactly the function. Example: compute partial sums for ex and compare to the limit; highlight the nonzero tail.
